title: Prepare repository for public release and add smoke test suite
body:
## Summary

This PR prepares the repository for public release by cleaning up legacy/unused code, fixing script execution bugs, adding a smoke test suite, and updating documentation.

### Key Changes
- **Repository Cleanup**:
  - Renamed `decoder_by_matrix` directory to `decoders` and updated all dependent imports.
  - Removed deprecated and unused artifacts (`simons_algorithm`, `shor.py`, `single_surface.py`, legacy PDF/markdown notes).
  - Cleaned up duplicate Golay code implementations and large state fixtures.
  - Removed orphaned surface code test files.
- **Script & Serialization Fixes**:
  - Fixed argument and signature compatibility across Cirq experiment scripts (`simple_measurement`, `universal_cnot`, `universal_hadamard`, `universal_t`, `deutsch_josza`).
  - Updated `custom_json_resolver` to resolve `cirq_experiments.conditions` and modern serialization hooks.
  - Extended `Analyzer` to support both Clifford and full state-vector simulations.
- **Test Suite & CI Optimizations**:
  - Added dedicated smoke test suites for Cirq scripts and Stim `simulate_cx` workflows.
  - Registered and tagged long-running simulation tests with `@pytest.mark.slow` and `@pytest.mark.very_slow` markers in `pyproject.toml`.
- **Documentation**:
  - Added paper BibTeX citation section to `README.md`.

title: fix(test): use spawn context in test_multiprocessing_basic_classical_control_fails
body:
## Problem

`test_multiprocessing_basic_classical_control_fails` was failing because it expected a `KeyError` that was never raised.

### Root cause

`cirq.MeasurementKey` caches its hash in a `_hash` dataclass field. When a key is pickled from the parent process and sent to a subprocess, that cached hash travels with it. In a subprocess with a **different hash seed** (i.e. `spawn`), the stale `_hash` points to the wrong bucket in the dict, causing a `KeyError` when cirq tries to look up the key in `_measurement_types`.

On **Linux the default start method is `fork`**, which clones the parent's entire memory space — including the same hash seed. The cached `_hash` is therefore always valid in the child, so no `KeyError` is raised and the test fails.

The test was originally written against `spawn` semantics (or an environment where hash randomization differed per process).

## Fix

Explicitly use `multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Pool` in `test_multiprocessing_basic_classical_control_fails` so the bug is reliably reproduced regardless of the system default start method. Added a docstring explaining the fork/spawn distinction.

title: Implement CX via Hadamard + ZZ measurement in UniversalTFaultTolerant
body:
## Summary

Replaces the `UniversalControlledOperation`-based CX in `_cx_code_to_tetrahedral` with a measurement-based implementation.

## Changes

The new `_cx_code_to_tetrahedral` performs a CX from the data encoding to the tetrahedral helper via:

1. **Hadamard on target** — applies `UniversalHadamard` to the tetrahedral encoding, putting it in the X basis
2. **Joint ZZ measurement** — measures the logical Z of the control and logical Z of the target as a single joint observable, yielding their parity
3. **Classically-controlled X on target** — applies logical X on the tetrahedral conditioned on the ZZ parity result being 1

This is equivalent to a CX gate via the standard teleportation-based measurement protocol.

## Cleanup

- Removed `UniversalControlledOperation` import and `_universal_controlled_operation_type` property (no longer needed)
- Added `_universal_hadamard_type` property pulling from `configuration.universal_hadamard_type`
- Replaced `TargetEncoding` import with `LogicalEncodingIndex`
